evidence.quote: it was mediaeval, so that Rubens seemed modern
as a taste or a smell, it was education, but it was education only sensual.

adjudications.reason: The regress logic is weakened but not lost. 'Education went backward' still follows the paragraph on eighteenth-century London. The Antwerp material itself sets up 'sixteenth century alive' by calling the town 'mediaeval, so that Rubens seemed modern'. The kneeling-at-the-Cross close was cut, but the plan makes the Antwerp details optional and keeps only the purely sensual education, which survives. Restoring 20 words would also overshoot the target. This is a legitimate tradeoff.

evidence.quote: This could not be called education, for he had never so much as listened to the music.
and it was accidental, unintended, unforeseen.

adjudications.reason: The episode still works as the model of accidental education. V5's 'accidental, unintended, unforeseen' leads directly into it. V6's prison-wall image is intact, and 'without so much as his knowing' plus 'never so much as listened to the music' convey involuntariness. The 'overrated ... to be so easily followed' paradox reads as self-mockery without the flower sentence. The dependency phrase 'Beethoven had partly become intelligible to him' is preserved.

evidence.quote: The professor mumbled his comments; the students made, or seemed to make, notes;
as it flourished in the thirteenth century. To an American the result was worthless.
They went to the lectures, made notes, and read textbooks, but never pretended to take their professor seriously.

adjudications.reason: Paragraph 8 jumps from the abstract 'lecture system' straight to 'the result was worthless'. The only eyewitness image of the single lecture, the mumbling professor and the students who 'made, or seemed to make, notes', has gone. Paragraph 9 then says the students 'made notes' and never took the professor seriously, which echoes a scene that is no longer shown. A 13-word restoration fits the +11 budget.

evidence.quote: as though he had not always avoided high schools with singular antipathy.
As an episode in the search for education, this adventure smacked of Heine.

adjudications.reason: The plan does not require the 'foolish' ledger sentence. Ironic framing of the Gymnasium episode survives in 'as though he had not always avoided high schools with singular antipathy', 'The experiment was hazardous' and 'smacked of Heine'. Cutting the sentence is an acceptable compression tradeoff.

evidence.quote: nothing was left of the experiment except the ghost of the Civil Law

adjudications.reason: The referent of 'this' is recoverable from the paragraph's opening, 'nothing was left of the experiment', and 'Yet' marks the turn to by-products clearly enough. The required phrase 'by-products ... more valuable than staples' is intact.

remaining_concerns: The Antwerp paragraph loses its century-by-century regress and the kneeling-at-the-Cross cadence. This was accepted as an optional tradeoff, but restoring 'the next step took it back to the sixteenth' could be reconsidered if the word budget allows.
